<!-- pr-reviewer: 2eefe69e5d6796e3bbfd35b4be5130b7dc7b767c -->

Reviewed PR #2742 at head 2eefe69e5d6796e3bbfd35b4be5130b7dc7b767c. The trial merge with main was clean. Built locally on the merged tree: camcraft-motion lib 451 passed / 0 failed (includes the four grid parity and superset tests), clippy clean (-D warnings), app `golden_cl` 33 passed and `operations` 120 passed / 0 failed - the toolpaths do not change, as the body says.

**The superset law holds by construction.** A facet lands in every cell its padded box touches; the query reads the one cell that holds the point; both use the same cell map (subtract, divide, floor, clamp - each step non-decreasing in IEEE-754), so box-holds-point gives same-cell bit for bit. Each cell lists its facets in ascending original index, once each (the CSR fill walks facets in index order). Each scan keeps its own box reject. The grid therefore visits a subset of the full scan's facets, in the same order, with the same code: the answers keep the same bits. `near()` falls back to the full scan on a non-finite box, a non-finite query point, a bad size, or an out-of-range index - never a guessed cell. The mutation note in the body (a 2% cell miss fails two tests) matches the test law: `grid_candidates_hold_every_facet_whose_box_holds_the_point` checks order, no duplicates and the superset on random, border and box-edge queries.

**Honesty check (the REQ ask).** The body says the grid gives no measurable gain, with the two timed runs (13.161 s / 13.908 s and 162.915 s / 161.515 s). The decision file `docs/decisions/2619-facet-grid.md` carries the same table and the same words: "The grid gives no measurable gain on this job." The two agree line for line. The follow-up it promises is filed: #2743 profiles the real hot path. The stated reason to merge anyway (the CPU reference for the GPU filter of #2526, O(n) build, unchanged output) is sound.

**Other checks.** Files under 400 lines. The non-point scans keep whole-set loops through `Deref` - verified in `flat.rs`, `shadow.rs`, `raster.rs`, `rings.rs`. `build_sups` returns the `SupSet` (grid built once per facet set, not per query - the cache rule holds). The lib-test placement is right: the scans are `pub(super)`, so `crates/motion/tests/` cannot reach them; the decision file records that deviation from the issue's wording.

Effort: high, safety floor (drop-cutter support = gouge path). P4, not P1 - no second review required.

Verdict: **merge-ready**.

Merge class: SAME. The head is `2eefe69e5d6796e3bbfd35b4be5130b7dc7b767c`, the head that the review names (comment 7005569714). No commit came after that review. The PR merges cleanly with `main`. This merge relies on that review. The issue is P4, so one collaborator review is sufficient.
